sections.heading: B06 Smaller Plates (reaction Short)
sections.sub: No big celebrity on video says it. This is the real source of the line you remember: the Profit First author.
sections.label: Reaction Short

items.t: Profit First Author Says Get Smaller Plates. He's Right.
items.src: TEDx Talks, Mike Michalowicz, "Profit first is better for entrepreneurs than G.A.A.P."
items.words: Starts on "he said what we need to do for health is get smaller plates". Ends on "with his wooden teeth".
items.what: Mike Michalowicz, author of Profit First, repeats what a fitness expert told him: smaller plates. He uses it as the analogy for his money system.
pts: Lesson: buy smaller plates; the same portion looks like a meal.
items.note: Not a household name. Alternate if you want a celebrity: Wendy Williams, Entertainment Tonight KyiVs3iS-P0 (not yet checked).

sections.heading: D15 Should You Train to Failure?
sections.sub: Cutler confirmed. No clip of Clavicular saying to leave one rep in the tank was found; the closest is below.
sections.label: Long reaction

items.t: Jay Cutler Never Trained To Failure
items.src: Renaissance Periodization, "Jay Cutler Never Trained to Failure"
items.words: Starts on "Jay Cutler was on a podcast". Ends on "I never trained to failure ever in my career".
items.what: Dr. Mike sets it up, then Cutler's own line.
pts: Lesson: failure depends on who you are; Cutler's failure is real failure.

items.t: Greg Doucette Mocks Clavicular's Training
items.src: Greg Doucette, "Juicing My Pants Reviewing Clavicular's Workout"
items.words: Starts on "Bro goes to the gym, does sets of four, maybe five reps". Ends on "only trains once a month".
items.what: Doucette's words about Clavicular, not Clavicular's own. Stand-in until a real Clavicular clip is found.
pts: Lesson: most guys who think they hit failure have five reps left.
items.note: Not Clavicular speaking. Tell me if you know where he said it.

sections.heading: D05 Arguments Against Zepbound
sections.sub: Each card is one objection. Note: three Jillian Michaels clips; you passed on her once as boring.
sections.label: Long reaction

items.t: Objection 1: Muscle loss: 40% of the weight lost is lean mass.
items.src: Bikman, Diary Of A CEO Clips
items.words: Starts on "for every six pounds of fat a person was losing". Ends on "including muscle and bone".
items.what: Muscle loss: 40% of the weight lost is lean mass.
pts: Lesson: half true; lift every day and eat protein first.

items.t: Objection 2: You'll gain it all back.
items.words: Starts on "you can't get off of it ever". Ends on "yo-yo dieting on crack".
items.what: You'll gain it all back.
pts: Lesson: true if you quit cold; stay on a low dose.

items.t: Objection 3: Fix your diet instead, plus side effects.
items.words: Starts on "You can lose weight by eating less". Ends on "vision problems".
items.what: Fix your diet instead, plus side effects.
pts: Lesson: I fixed my diet and still sat at 190 for a year.

items.t: Objection 4: It stops working.
items.words: Starts on "now we're 18 months into it and you will plateau". Ends on "let me Google that for you".
items.what: It stops working.
pts: Lesson: it's a dial: raise the dose a step and eat a little less.

items.t: Objection 5: It makes you want to do everything less.
items.words: Starts on "the EU is right now investigating". Ends on "makes you want to do everything less".
items.what: It makes you want to do everything less.
pts: Lesson: true, and that's the point: less alcohol, less sugar.

items.t: Objection 6: Cost.
items.words: Starts on "we're spending $1600 a month on this drug". Ends on "$3 trillion a year".
items.what: Cost.
pts: Lesson: price it the way you buy it.

items.t: Objection 7: It's a lifelong drug.
items.words: Starts on "this is on the box, a lifetime drug". Ends on "lifetime recurring annuity".
items.what: It's a lifelong drug.
pts: Lesson: true, and fine: a low dose for life.

items.t: Objection 8: You'll stop wanting to exercise.
items.src: Bikman, Diary Of A CEO Clips
items.words: Starts on "you also are not interested as much in exercise". Ends on "drinking with the boys".
items.what: You'll stop wanting to exercise.
pts: Lesson: wrong for me: seven days a week.

items.t: Objection 9: Eat better instead of taking a drug.
items.words: Starts on "in Denmark they do not recommend it". Ends on "so addicted to drugs".
items.what: Eat better instead of taking a drug.
pts: Lesson: the drug is what made eating better stick.

items.t: Objection 10: It's cheating.
items.words: Starts on "we can facilitate 15% weight loss". Ends on "diarrhea, constipation".
items.what: It's cheating.
pts: Lesson: a tool is not cheating.

items.t: Rule 1: If you can't do it for a decade, don't do it for a day.
items.words: Starts on "there's a few things that matter". Ends on "don't do it for a day".
items.what: If you can't do it for a decade, don't do it for a day.
pts: Lesson: pick habits you can keep for ten years.

items.t: Rule 2: One gram of protein per pound.
items.words: Starts on "here's step three, you multiply your weight". Ends on "means 200 grams of protein".
items.what: One gram of protein per pound.
pts: Lesson: about 0.6 grams per pound is enough.

items.t: Rule 3: Cutting calories = body weight x 10.
items.words: Starts on "let's say I'm a 200 lb guy". Ends on "2,000 calories".
items.what: Cutting calories = body weight x 10.
pts: Lesson: your verdict.

items.t: Rule 4: Hit protein first, the rest is free.
items.words: Starts on "here's the magic of how this works". Ends on "that's 880 calories".
items.what: Hit protein first, the rest is free.
pts: Lesson: eat the protein first at every meal.

items.t: Rule 5: Same breakfast and lunch every day.
items.words: Starts on "I eat the same breakfast and lunch every day". Ends on "grab a Quest Bar at the airport".
items.what: Same breakfast and lunch every day.
pts: Lesson: decide your meals before you're hungry.

items.t: Rule 6: Track what you eat.
items.words: Starts on "if you don't track what you eat". Ends on "you don't even have data".
items.what: Track what you eat.
pts: Lesson: weigh in every morning.

items.t: Rule 7: Two pounds of meat a day, dessert on top.
items.words: Starts on "I eat two pounds of meat a day". Ends on "dessert in excess of my calories".
items.what: Two pounds of meat a day, dessert on top.
pts: Lesson: your verdict.

items.t: Rule 8: Progressive overload on machines.
items.words: Starts on "training has been progressive overload". Ends on "almost two decades".
items.what: Progressive overload on machines.
pts: Lesson: machines and cables, not barbells.
